scope: Read-only bounded priority/applicability scout; hand inferences explicitly separated from source statements.

output.summary: Literature search run 2026-10-19 (bounded; priority and theorem-applicability only). Correctness is taken from the recorded verdicts and was not re-checked. RESULT: no published theorem that I located implies SLZ3 for floor(2p/3)+1<=kappa<=p-2, or LS, LS+ or STAB. None gives a counterexample either. Not finding a source is not evidence of novelty. EARLIER RESULTS AND ROUTINE PIECES: (1) At the kappa=p-1 endpoint, SLZ3 and LS+ follow at once from the classical s_2p(C_p)=3p-1 (EGZ applied twice). Under (ZP_(p-1)) every odd Y already has |Y|<=3p-2=3kappa+1. (2) SLZ3 Steps 4/6/7 are routine given Zeng-Yuan 2011 (already credited). (3) NEW, correcting the earlier screen's FB row. The proof of Savchev-Chen 2008 Thm 5 contains a balance-and-room inequality (3). It concerns a maximum-length zero subsequence against a zero-free complement of length >n/2. Moved word for word to odd sequences, it gives ZSTRUCT's bound s_i<=slack and Lemma FB's W+S(N)<=2p-1 whenever L>=p+1 [INFERENCE, hand-checked, not reviewed]. FB-p sits exactly at the boundary l=n/2, where that argument's final contradiction n>=2l degenerates. FB-p's additions (the S(p) normalisation, realisation with the exceptional family g^(p-1)(pg), and the W=p case via the no-2p-zero-sum hypothesis) are a bounded delta with no source located. So is EXT's one-term extension. INAPPLICABLE RANGES: every published n-zero-free structure theorem needs length >=3p-1 at n=2p. That covers SC2008 (>3n/2-1), Peng-Qian-Sun-Wang 2014 (n+floor(n/2)-1) and Gao-Li-Yuan-Zhuang 2015 Cor 9 (>=n+n/p+p-2). Odd sequences with no 2p-term zero-sum have length <=3p-2, so those statements never apply here. TOOL: a classical Cauchy-Davenport / DeVos-Goddyn-Mohar count shows that LS's threshold p+2kappa+1 is exactly where a unique odd generator of multiplicity >=|Y|-p+2>=2kappa+3 is forced [INFERENCE]. It says nothing at the LS+ lengths 3kappa+2..p+2kappa. PARTIALS: TV, RED+, SHIFT, MAX and STAB=>LS+ are routine. SLZ3 re-runs S1-sharp's proof and carries the same unlocated delta. STRONGEST MISSING ASSUMPTION: STAB itself, i.e. an inverse statement at ambient length 3kappa+1. Equivalently: an odd-coset, length-window analogue of SC2008 Thm 5 saying that (ZP_kappa) and length >=3kappa+2 (or >=p+2kappa+1 for LS) imply Y=alpha u beta with L(alpha)<2p and L(1-beta)<=2kappa. That decomposition yields (S1_kappa) through SC2008 Prop 4(a). STAB must exclude kappa=p-1: 1^21 5^10 in Z_22 is a counterexample there [INFERENCE].

findings.claim: SC2008 Thm 5: for length >3n/2-1, a sequence is n-zero-free iff it is similar to alpha u beta with L(alpha)<n and L(1-beta)<n. At n=2p this needs length >=3p. Odd C_2p sequences with no 2p-term zero-sum have length <=3p-2. So the statement never applies to FB, FB-p, EXT, LS, LS+ or STAB.
findings.quote: A sequence of length greater than 3n/2−1 in the cyclic group Z_n does not contain an n-term zero subsequence if and only if it is similar to the union of two sequences α and β
findings.source: S. Savchev, F. Chen, Long n-zero-free sequences in finite cyclic groups, Discrete Math. 308 (2008) 1-8, Zbl 1165.11026
findings.date_version: arXiv math/0604356v1, 2006-04-16; journal version not read
findings.scope: all sequences over Z_n, up to affine similarity (translations included)

findings.claim: The key step of SC2008 Thm 5 works as follows. Take a maximum-length zero subsequence sigma=1^w b_1...b_q against the zero-free rest tau, with |tau|=l>n/2 and L(tau)=S<n. Then every v_j=-b_j satisfies v_j<n-S, and L(tau)+sum v_j<n. Set sigma=Z (a longest zero-sum), tau=Y-Z, g->1, v_j=s_i, w=n+. The two conclusions become ZSTRUCT's s_i<=slack and Lemma FB's W+S(N)<=2p-1, hence S(N)=n+. The argument uses only: maximality of sigma, zero-freeness of tau, l>n/2, L(tau)<n, and Prop 3 (needs 2l>S). All of these hold in FB's setting (S') with L>=p+1. Neither n-zero-freeness nor the 3n/2 length is used. So Lemma FB (L>=p+1) is routine given this proof. FB's own proof (unit exchange) is different.
findings.quote: The following inequality stronger than L(τ) < n implies the conclusion directly: L(τ) + Σ_{j=1}^{q} −b_j < n. (3) … It follows from the observation that n − v_j > S, j = 1,…,q.
findings.read_scope: Sec 3, pp. 6-7, read line by line
findings.verified: Primary source read; the Sigma glyph was restored. The transfer to odd sequences is [INFERENCE], hand-checked and not reviewed.
findings.scope: odd C_2p sequences; Z a longest zero-sum; complement of length L>=p+1 with an index-<1 generator

findings.claim: The transferred argument breaks exactly at l=n/2=p. Four of its steps need l>n/2: 2l-S>=2; T>1 (via 2l-n>=1); the final contradiction n>=2l; and n-2S<0. FB-p's L=p case is therefore outside the transfer. FB-p closes it with: S(p); a realisation step with the exceptional family g^(p-1)(pg); FB's unit exchange, which still works at L=p when W>=p+2; and the no-2p-zero-sum hypothesis when W=p. SC2008 says the characterisation cannot be extended below its range. Its examples (0^(n-1)2^(n/2-1)3) contain even elements, though, so they say nothing about odd sequences [INFERENCE].
findings.quote: S + 1 ≤ … ≤ n − (2ℓ − S − 1) = (n − 2ℓ) + S + 1, implying n ≥ 2ℓ which is a contradiction.
findings.source: Savchev-Chen 2008, Sec 3 and the end of Sec 3 (range remark)

findings.claim: In the proof of SC2008 Prop 4(a), every zero subsequence gamma of a separable alpha u beta has |gamma|<=r+|beta|, with r<=sum a_i=sum(-b_j). Hence |gamma|<=L(1-beta) [INFERENCE]. FB-p case (N) is literally such a decomposition, with no translation [INFERENCE]: alpha=Y'g^(n+) with L(alpha)=W+n+<=2p-1, and beta=N with L(1-beta)=sum(1+s_i)=|Z|=2t. So (S1_kappa) follows from separability with L(1-beta)<=2kappa. That is the natural target form for LS and LS+.
findings.quote: Therefore r ≤ Σ a_i = Σ −b_j < n − |β|, implying r + |β| < n. Since |γ| ≤ r + |β|, we infer that α ∪ β is n-zero-free.
findings.verified: read; the length bound and the FB-p identification are [INFERENCE]
findings.scope: any alpha u beta over Z_n

findings.claim: Classical inverse results for n-zero-free sequences of length 2n-2 (Peterson-Yuster; Bialostocki-Dierker) and 2n-3 (Ordaz-Flores) are restated in SC2008. Read in C_p language with n=p, they constrain the complement S-A of any p-term zero-sum A in a sequence of length 3p-3 or 3p-2 that has no 2p-term zero-sum. Those are the lengths of LS at kappa=p-2. This is a possible route, not an implication; it was not carried out.
findings.quote: each n-zero-free sequence of length 2n−3, n > 4, is similar to 0^{n−1}1^{n−2} or 0^{n−1}1^{n−3}2.
findings.scope: C_p, p-term zero-sums; the parity and window hypotheses are not handled

findings.claim: The n-zero-free inverse problem at length n+floor(n/2)-1 is solved; at n=2p that is length 3p-1. Odd sequences cannot reach that length (they stop at 3p-2), so the result is vacuous here. The zbMATH summary attributes the k>=floor(n/2)+1 characterisation to SC Discrete Math. 307 (2007). SC2008's own abstract places it in Discrete Math. 308. This looks like a citation mix-up and does not matter here.
findings.quote: characterized all the n-zero-sum free sequences of length n+k−1 over G, where ⌊n/2⌋+1≤k<n. In the present paper, we determine all the n-zero-sum free sequences of length n+⌊n/2⌋−1 over G.
findings.source: J. Peng, G. Qian, F. Sun, L. Wang, Int. J. Number Theory 10 (2014) 1991-2009, DOI 10.1142/S1793042114500663

findings.claim: The GLYZ structure theorem for n-zero-free sequences needs length >=n+n/p+p-2. At n=2p the smallest prime is 2, so the length must be >=3p: vacuous here. GLYZ Thms 3-4 (long zero-free sequences of length between n/3 and n/2) assume odd n>=50, so they do not apply to n=2p.
findings.quote: Let p be the smallest prime dividing n, and S be an n-zero-sum free sequence over Z_n of length |S| = n + ℓ, where ℓ ≥ n/p + p − 2 is an integer.
findings.source: W. Gao, Y. Li, P. Yuan, J. Zhuang, Arch. Math. 105 (2015) 361-370, Cor 9 / Thm 8 / Thm 3
findings.date_version: author preprint dated 2015-05-07; journal version not read

findings.claim: GLYZ Lemma 5 restates the DeVos-Goddyn-Mohar theorem. For prime p it is just Cauchy-Davenport applied to a set partition. Take G=C_p and l=2kappa+2; (ZP_kappa) forbids a zero sum of l terms. Then sum_x min(2kappa+2, v_x)<=p+2kappa. Consequence for any (ZP_kappa) Y with |Y|>=p+2kappa+1: exactly one odd generator g has v_g(Y)>=|Y|-p+2>=2kappa+3. Every other value has multiplicity <=2kappa+2, and |Y-g^v|<=p-2. The involution p is excluded because p^(2kappa+2) is a zero-sum inside the window [INFERENCE]. LS's threshold p+2kappa+1 is exactly where this count starts to work. It gives nothing for |Y|<=p+2kappa, hence nothing at LS+ lengths. The 96h LS/LS+ files never use it (grep found no match); the 2026-10-16 lane used Bollobas-Leader in a different setting.
findings.quote: Let ℓ be a positive integer, S be a sequence over a finite abelian group G, and let H = stab(Σ_ℓ(S)). Then, |Σ_ℓ(S)| ≥ |H|(1 − ℓ + Σ_{Q∈G/H} min{ℓ, v_Q(S)}).
findings.source: GLYZ 2015, Lemma 5, citing DeVos-Goddyn-Mohar, Adv. Math. 220 (2009) 1531-1548
findings.verified: Secondary statement read, glyphs restored. The DGM primary source was not read. The application is [INFERENCE].
findings.scope: an available tool; implies neither LS nor LS+

findings.claim: Zeng-Yuan 2011: a zero-sum sequence of length >=2floor(n/2)+2 with at most two atoms has a generator whose coefficients sum to 2n. This makes SLZ3 Steps 4/6/7 routine; SLZ3 Step 2 supplies the two-atom hypothesis. Steps 1-3, 5, 8-9 and the 3kappa+1 bound are not covered.
findings.quote: let S∈F(G) be a zero-sum sequence of length |S|≥2⌊n/2⌋+2. Suppose that S can be decomposed into a product of at most two minimal zero-sum sequences.

findings.claim: For n=2p (smallest non-divisor 3), Berger-Wang give s'_2p(Z/2pZ)=4p-2. Odd zero-sum sequences without a 2p-term zero-sum already have length <=3p-2, so this value is vacuous here.
findings.quote: Theorem 1.3. The modified EGZ constant of Z/nZ is given by s′nt(Z/nZ) = (t + 1)n − ℓ + 1, where ℓ is the smallest integer such that ℓ ∤ n.
findings.source: A. Berger, D. Wang, Modified Erdos-Ginzburg-Ziv constants for Z/nZ and (Z/nZ)^2

findings.claim: Berger-Wang define the modified constant s'_L(G0) for a subset G0 and a set of lengths L. Let G0 be the odd coset of C_2p and L the even lengths in [2floor(2p/3)+2, 2p]. Then S1-sharp is equivalent to s'_L(G0)=2floor(2p/3)+2 [INFERENCE]. SLZ3 is equivalent to: every odd zero-sum sequence of length >=3kappa+2 has a proper zero-sum subsequence of length >=2kappa+2 [INFERENCE]. The only computed values I found are for G0=G with L a single length (this paper) and for integer intervals (Augspurger et al., arXiv 1603.03978, not read). None covers a coset or a length window.
findings.quote: the modified Erdös–Ginzburg–Ziv constant s′L(G0), defined as the smallest ℓ such that any zero-sum sequence of length at least ℓ with elements in G0 contains a zero-sum subsequence whose length is in L.

findings.claim: The classical formula s_(k exp G)(G)=k exp(G)+D(G)-1 for k exp(G)>=|G| gives s_2p(C_p)=3p-1. Elementary proof: apply EGZ twice. Write odd elements as (1,x) in C_2+C_p: a 2p-term subsequence is zero-sum iff its x-sum is 0 in C_p. So (ZP_(p-1)) forces |Y|<=3p-2=3kappa+1. Hence SLZ3 and LS+ at kappa=p-1 are immediate corollaries of a classical result. The lane already noted this for LS+; the SLZ3 verdict did not.
findings.quote: There are several results on this constant, such as s_{k exp(G)}(G)=k exp(G)+D(G)−1 if k exp(G)≥|G|
findings.source: zbMATH review of W. Gao, D. Han, J. Peng, F. Sun, J. Combin. Theory Ser. A 125 (2014) 240-253
findings.verified: read; the EGZ-twice argument is elementary

findings.claim: Gao-Panigrahi-Thangadurai: a sequence over Z_p of length 2p-k with no p-term zero-sum has two values a, b with multiplicities u+v>=2p-2k+2, when 2<=k<=[(p+1)/3]+1. Apply it in C_p language to S-A, where S is an LS+ candidate of length 3kappa+2 and A is any p-term zero-sum. That is the case k=3e-2 with e=p-kappa. The result applies when 3e-2<=[(p+1)/3]+1 and gives two values with combined multiplicity >=2p-6e+6. Only partial structure; nothing is implied [INFERENCE].
findings.quote: Let S = (a_1,a_2,...,a_{2p-k}) be any sequence in Z_p such that there is no subsequence of length p of S whose sum is zero … where u ≥ v, u+v ≥ 2p−2k+2
findings.source: W. D. Gao, A. Panigrahi, R. Thangadurai, Proc. Indian Acad. Sci. Math. Sci. 115 (2005) 67-77
findings.scope: C_p, p-term zero-sums; parity and window not handled

findings.claim: Savchev-Chen 2007 (index <1 for zero-free sequences of length >n/2) is the source of the normalisation used in FB and EXT. EXT's t0=0 case is exactly this theorem. The boundary length n/2 needs S(p) (a prior import; not duplicated here).
findings.quote: for each zero-free sequence (a_i) of length ℓ>n/2 in Z_n there is an integer g coprime to n such that if … then Σ ga_i < n.
findings.source: S. Savchev, F. Chen, Discrete Math. 307 (2007) 2671-2679
findings.date_version: arXiv math/0602568 (2006-02-25); later versions not checked

findings.claim: Zeng-Yuan 2023 study the inverse problem for sequences with no zero-sum of length <=h(S). That is a short-zero-sum invariant, not a length window near 2p, and it does not imply any lane statement.
findings.quote: It is interesting to study the corresponding inverse problem, that is to find information on the structure of the sequence S which does not contain zero-sum subsequences of length at most h(S).
findings.source: X. Zeng, P. Yuan, Electron. J. Combin. 30(4) (2023) #P4.21

findings.claim: Hui-Li 2025 classify sequences whose zero-sum subsequences all have one length, in rank 2. A different hypothesis and group; it does not apply.
findings.quote: we characterize the structure of sequences S over G = C_n ⊕ C_{nm} (where m≥2) when |S| = disc(G)− 1 and all nonempty zero-sum subsequences of S have the same length.

theorem_comparison.setting: Odd elements of Z_2p are the elements (1,x) of C_2+C_p. A subsequence of length l is zero-sum iff l is even and its C_p-coordinates sum to 0. Consequently (ZP_kappa) always forbids 2p-term zero-sums, and the classical bound |Y|<=3p-2 holds for every kappa<=p-1.
exact_statements: SLZ3 (accepted; proof-SLZ3-v1.md:15-18, erratum-1 M5/M7): p>=5 prime, floor(2p/3)+1<=kappa<=p-1, Y odd with (ZP_kappa). Then every shortest long zero-sum T of Y satisfies |T|<=3kappa+1. Equivalently, an odd (ZP_kappa) zero-sum T with |T|>=3kappa+2 has a proper long zero-sum. Bounds |T| only, not |Y|.

EXT (accepted; proof-SLZ-EXT-v2.md:21-23): Y1 satisfies (S1_kappa) with a longest zero-sum of length 2t0, |Y1|>=p+2kappa and L=|Y1|-2t0>=p+1. If Y1 y satisfies (ZP_kappa), then Y1 y satisfies (S1_kappa).
FB (accepted earlier; proof-FB-v1.md:19-20): in setting (S') with L>=p+1, S(N)<=2p-1-W, hence S(N)=n+ and W+n+<=2p-1.

FB-p (accepted; proof-KPS-v4.md:27-33): Y has no 2p-zero-sum, Z is a longest zero-sum with |Z|=2t, |Y-Z|=p, and g normalises Y-Z (W<=2p-1). Then either (X) Y-Z=g^(p-1)(pg) and Z lies in {g,pg}, or (N) Z=g^(n+)N with N made of terms -s g (s odd, s<=min(2t-1, slack)), S(N)=n+ and W+n+<=2p-1.
LS+ (conjecture; LSplus-scope-v1.md:11, range floor(2p/3)+1<=kappa<=p-2): (ZP_kappa) and not (S1_kappa) imply |Y|<=3kappa+1.
STAB (conjecture; proof-LSplus-partials-v2-addendum-MAX-v2.md:28): every (ZP_kappa) non-(S1_kappa) Y of length exactly 3kappa+1 is E2=h^(3kappa-p+2)(3h)^(p-1) or E3=h^(3kappa-2p+2)(3h)^(2p-1).

Unreviewed candidates: TV (proof-LSplus-partials-v2.md:16-20); RED+ (:42-50); SHIFT (:52-55); MAX and STAB=>LS+ (addendum-MAX-v2.md:10-12, 28-32). Successor directory continuations/stab-round2 was empty at read time.

implication_table.to: FB, FB-p, EXT, LS, LS+, STAB
implication_table.why: needs length >=3p; odd sequences have length <=3p-2

implication_table.to: Lemma FB (L>=p+1) and ZSTRUCT's slack bound
implication_table.why: uses only maximality, zero-freeness, l>n/2 and L(tau)<n
the contradiction n>=2l degenerates at l=n/2

implication_table.to: normalisation in FB/EXT; EXT t0=0; FB-p at L=p

implication_table.why: forces a dominant generator with v>=|Y|-p+2 at LS lengths; LS itself is not derived
lengths 3kappa+1..p+2kappa lie below the count threshold
the computed value (4p-2) is vacuous; the needed coset/window values are not computed

implication_table.to: LS, LS+ for kappa near p-1
implication_table.why: constrain complements of p-term zero-sums in C_p; parity and window untreated
short zero-sums, equal-length zero-sums, or non-divisible lengths
(ZP_10) holds (4j=0 mod 22 forces j in {0,11}); 1^19 5^5 is a long zero-sum (sum 44, length 24); length 31=3kappa+1; the sequence is not E2 or E3. So STAB's restriction kappa<=p-2 is necessary.

partials_assessment: SLZ3: routine re-run of the accepted S1-sharp, replacing three uses of p>=3delta-1 by N>=3kappa+2. The kappa=p-1 endpoint is classical. For floor(2p/3)+1<=kappa<=p-2 the bounded delta with no source located equals S1-sharp's (Steps 1-3, 5, 8-9 counting), minus the Zeng-Yuan steps. Sharp only at kappa=floor(2p/3)+1.

FB-p: case (N) is a translation-free SC2008-type separable decomposition. The SC2008 mechanism covers L>=p+1 (that is FB); FB-p's extra is the l=n/2 boundary: S(p) normalisation, realisation with exceptional family (X) (compare the smoothness exception in GLYZ Thm 11), and W=p via no 2p-zero-sum. Technical, bounded delta, no source located.
EXT: the t0=0 case is Savchev-Chen 2007. For t0>=1 (preserving (S1), i.e. separability, under one added term given (ZP_kappa)) no analogue was located. Bounded delta.
FB (from the earlier round): the conclusion is routine given SC2008's proof [INFERENCE]. This is a priority correction only; correctness is unaffected.

LS+ partials TV, RED+, SHIFT, MAX and STAB=>LS+: elementary arithmetic and short reductions from SLZ3 and S1-sharp. Routine scaffolding, nothing to credit on its own. Same for the propagation candidates EXT', EXT-p, PROP+ and PAIR.

strongest_missing_assumption.LS_plus: Rule out a (ZP_kappa) non-(S1) Y of length exactly 3kappa+2; RED+(a) shows that suffices. STAB(p,kappa) together with MAX would do it.
strongest_missing_assumption.STAB_by_induction: Two pieces are missing. (i) Three-occurrence deletion: every length-(3kappa+1) (ZP_kappa) non-(S1) Y has 3 occurrences meeting every 2kappa-zero-sum while some long zero-sum survives. (ii) Classification of the 3-term (ZP_kappa)-extensions of E2(kappa-1) and E3(kappa-1); the unreviewed one-term notes find only h, -h and -3h. A separate base case STAB(floor(2p/3)+1) is also needed.
strongest_missing_assumption.equivalent_single_lemma: SEP_kappa: every odd (ZP_kappa) Y of length >=3kappa+2 (or >=p+2kappa+1 for LS) equals alpha u beta for some odd generator, with L(alpha)<2p and L(1-beta)<=2kappa. This is an odd-coset, length-window analogue of SC2008 Thm 5, whose published range (>=3p) these sequences cannot reach. SEP gives (S1) through Prop 4(a) [INFERENCE].
strongest_missing_assumption.LS: The PAIR obstruction (notes-LS-propagation-v1.md:69-71, unreviewed) must be excluded at length p+2kappa+1. The Cauchy-Davenport normal form is available there: Y=g^v R with v>=2kappa+3 and |R|<=p-2. Still missing is an SC2008-(3)-type exchange lemma that works under the window hypothesis.
strongest_missing_assumption.necessary_restrictions: STAB needs kappa<=p-2 (the 1^21 5^10 example). SLZ3 needs kappa<=p-1 (g^(4p) at kappa=p). (ZP) and (S1) differ only for kappa>floor(2p/3) (F1).

significance.rubric: Major would require either a new method, solving a prominent problem (ordered Olson for D_2p), or a matched-assumption improvement over a published bound. None of these is established here.
significance.SLZ3: Modest extension: a sharp specialist length bound. At kappa=p-1 it is an immediate corollary of a classical result.
significance.FB: Routine given SC2008's proof [INFERENCE]. The statement itself was not located.
significance.LS_LSplus_STAB_if_proved: Potentially substantive specialist inputs to ordered Olson for D_2p; major not established.

counterpoints: The FB-from-SC2008 transfer, the Cauchy-Davenport normal form, the s'_L equivalences and the kappa=p-1 counterexample are my own hand derivations and have not been reviewed. Check them independently before changing any credit wording.

FB's own unit-exchange proof differs from SC2008's argument. It is what lets FB-p handle W>=p+2 at L=p, where SC2008's inequality becomes an equality, so FB's method adds something small at the boundary.
The Cauchy-Davenport normal form might make LS routine through an SC2008-type exchange; this was not checked. A specialist could judge LS routine.

Bounded two-valued hand check at kappa=p-2: sequences 1^a c^b of length 3kappa+1 that satisfy (ZP) but not (S1) are exactly E2 (c=3) and E3 (c=3^-1). The cases c=-1 and c=p satisfy (S1). This supports STAB but is not literature.
The lane's probes are small (p<=11), so they are aids only.

Dropped as different invariants: Products of k atoms II (rho_k); Gao-Geroldinger 2009; Gao-Li-Peng-Plyley-Wang 2011 (Lemke-Kleitman); Han-Zhang 2018 (p-groups); Gao-Han-Peng-Sun 2014 (direct constants); Multiplicative Property II (rank 2); Zhao 2025 (s_<=k).
